source.board: National Board of Examiners in Optometry (NBEO)
source.qualification: NBEO examination content outline and ASCO curriculum model
source.document: Published exam blueprint and optometric education curriculum areas
source.track: professional · doctor of optometry curriculum/exam structure

optometry.note: Units follow the NBEO/ASCO curriculum arc — basic visual science first, then refraction and dispensing, then ocular disease and the systemic connections.

lesson.title: Optics for Optometry
lesson.summary: Light as the clinician's raw material — refraction, prisms and the aberrations glasses must fight.

lesson.title: Ocular Anatomy and Physiology
lesson.summary: The eye as an optical instrument and a piece of the brain — cornea to visual cortex.

lesson.title: Refraction and Binocular Vision
lesson.summary: Prescribing clarity — the refraction routine and the two-eye coordination problems of childhood.

lesson.title: Lenses and Dispensing
lesson.summary: The technology of correction — spectacles, contacts, multifocals and low-vision devices.

lesson.title: Ocular Disease
lesson.summary: The blinding four — glaucoma's silent pressure, cataract, macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease.

lesson.title: The Eye as a Systemic Window
lesson.summary: What the fundus reveals — hypertension, diabetes, thyroid disease and brain lesions visible in the eye.

lesson.title: Optometry in Public Health and Practice
lesson.summary: Vision as population health — screening, uncorrected-refraction burden and running an ethical practice.

source.qualification: CAPTE accreditation standards and APTA DPT curriculum content
source.document: Published accreditation standards' required content areas
source.track: professional · doctor of physical therapy curriculum

physiotherapy.note: Units follow the DPT curriculum's required content — the movement sciences first, then examination and the major clinical areas by system and population.

lesson.title: The Movement Sciences
lesson.summary: The scientific base of physio — biomechanics, exercise physiology and how movement is learned.

lesson.title: Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation
lesson.summary: The largest caseload — joints, tendons and the staged rehabilitation from injury to return.

lesson.title: Cardiorespiratory Physiotherapy
lesson.summary: Rehabilitating the chest — airway clearance, cardiac rehab and physio in intensive care.

lesson.title: Neurological Rehabilitation
lesson.summary: Re-training the injured nervous system — stroke recovery, neuroplasticity and task-specific training.

lesson.title: Exercise Prescription
lesson.summary: Exercise as a dose — loading principles, progression and the criteria for return to play.

lesson.title: Physiotherapy Across Populations
lesson.summary: Tailoring the science — children, older adults at risk of falls, and pelvic health.

lesson.title: Assessment and Clinical Reasoning
lesson.summary: The thinking physiotherapist — examination structure, test validity and measuring what matters.

lesson.title: Professional Physiotherapy Practice
lesson.summary: The profession's frame — ethics, evidence and the team around the patient.

source.document: Published accreditation standards' curriculum content areas

occupational-therapy.note: Units follow ACOTE's content areas — occupation-centred theory, the OT process, and practice across the lifespan and settings.

lesson.title: Occupation: the Core Construct
lesson.summary: Why 'occupation' means everything people do, not jobs — and how OT analyses any activity into its demands.

lesson.title: The Occupational Therapy Process
lesson.summary: From referral to discharge — assessment, client-centred goals and measuring change that matters.

lesson.title: Paediatric OT
lesson.summary: Occupation for children — play, sensory processing and the school as a practice setting.

lesson.title: Physical Rehabilitation OT
lesson.summary: Rebuilding daily life after injury — adaptive equipment, environmental design and re-training tasks.

lesson.title: OT in Mental Health
lesson.summary: The profession's roots — using occupation and relationship therapeutically in mental health.

lesson.title: Assistive Technology
lesson.summary: Technology as enabler — wheelchairs, communication devices and the smart home as therapy.

lesson.title: Professional OT Practice
lesson.summary: The OT's place in the team — ethics, evidence and advocating for occupation as health.

source.qualification: CAA Accreditation Standards for speech-language pathology

speech-therapy.note: Units follow ASHA's knowledge areas — the communicative sciences, development, and the disorders of speech, language, hearing and swallowing.

lesson.title: Speech and Hearing Sciences
lesson.summary: How speech is made and heard — articulators, sound waves and the audiogram.

lesson.title: Language Development
lesson.summary: How children crack language — milestones, bilingual advantage and the roots of reading.

lesson.title: Speech Sound Disorders
lesson.summary: When speech sounds go wrong — articulation, phonology, apraxia and structural causes.

lesson.title: Language Disorders Across the Lifespan
lesson.summary: From DLD in children to aphasia in adults — assessment and therapy for language breakdown.

lesson.title: Fluency, Voice and Resonance
lesson.summary: The speech subsystems — stuttering's nature and therapy, voice care and nasal resonance.

lesson.title: Dysphagia: Swallowing Disorders
lesson.summary: The other half of the job — swallowing anatomy, assessment and the safety of every meal.

lesson.title: AAC and Professional Practice
lesson.summary: Communication without speech — AAC systems, evidence and the profession's ethics.

radiography.note: Units follow the ARRT content domains — physics and equipment, patient care, image production, and procedures by anatomy.

lesson.title: X-ray Physics and Safety
lesson.summary: How X-rays are made, how they image, and the ALARA principle that governs every exposure.

lesson.title: Patient Care in Radiography
lesson.summary: Care before physics — consent, infection control and contrast-agent safety.

lesson.title: Image Production and Quality
lesson.summary: Making images that answer questions — digital receptors, positioning and what makes an image diagnostic.

lesson.title: Radiographic Procedures I
lesson.summary: The routine views — chest, abdomen, limbs and spine, and positioning under trauma conditions.

lesson.title: CT, MRI and Fluoroscopy
lesson.summary: Beyond the plain film — how cross-sectional imaging works and the radiographer's expanded role.

lesson.title: Radiation Biology and Protection
lesson.summary: Ionising radiation's biology — dose limits, justification and the culture of protection.

lesson.title: Professional Radiographic Practice
lesson.summary: The registered technologist's obligations — scope, ethics and the QA programme behind every department.

source.board: National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians (NREMT)
source.document: Official published cognitive exam domains and EMS scope of practice

paramedicine.note: Units follow the national paramedic curriculum's domains — preparation and pharmacology, assessment, and the medicine and trauma of pre-hospital care.

lesson.title: EMS Systems and the Paramedic
lesson.summary: Where paramedicine sits — response systems, crew safety and the law at the roadside.

lesson.title: Pre-hospital Drugs and Airway
lesson.summary: The paramedic's toolkit — emergency medications and definitive airway management in the field.

lesson.title: Pre-hospital Assessment
lesson.summary: Deciding in minutes — the survey sequence, monitoring and the paramedic's treatment priorities.

lesson.title: Cardiac Emergencies and Resuscitation
lesson.summary: Hearts in arrest — rhythm recognition, resuscitation algorithms and what happens after ROSC.

lesson.title: Medical Emergencies in the Field
lesson.summary: The medicine you meet on the street — diabetes, seizures, breathing, allergy and overdose.

lesson.title: Pre-hospital Trauma Care
lesson.summary: Golden-hour medicine — mechanism, bleeding control, shock and the load-and-go decision.

lesson.title: Special Populations and Major Incidents
lesson.summary: The hard cases — children, childbirth, the elderly, and command at a multi-casualty scene.

source.board: American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) Board of Certification
source.qualification: ASCP BOC Medical Laboratory Scientist content outline / NAACLS standards
source.document: Official published exam content outline by laboratory discipline

medical-laboratory-science.note: Units follow the BOC content areas — one per laboratory discipline, from blood banking through microbiology, plus operations and safety.

lesson.title: Laboratory Operations and Safety
lesson.summary: The lab before the lab — specimens, quality control and the biosafety that protects everyone.

lesson.title: Haematology and Coagulation
lesson.summary: Reading blood — cell counts, the anaemia and leukaemia patterns, and the clotting screen.

lesson.title: Clinical Chemistry
lesson.summary: Blood chemistry as diagnosis — metabolic panels, electrolytes and the analysers behind them.

lesson.title: Clinical Microbiology
lesson.summary: Growing and naming the enemy — cultures, susceptibility testing and rapid molecular methods.

lesson.title: Blood Banking and Transfusion
lesson.summary: The gift of blood, made safe — grouping, crossmatching and the investigation of reactions.

lesson.title: Immunology and Serology
lesson.summary: Immunity as measurable chemistry — antibody tests, autoimmunity and serological diagnosis.

lesson.title: Urinalysis and Molecular Diagnostics
lesson.summary: Old test, new science — the urinalysis workhorse and the molecular platforms reshaping the lab.

lesson.title: Laboratory Management and Informatics
lesson.summary: Running the diagnostic engine room — accreditation, LIS systems and the lab as teacher.

source.board: National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (NCEES)
source.qualification: NCEES FE Environmental CBT Exam Specifications

environmental-engineering.note: Units follow the NCEES FE Environmental specification's knowledge areas — water, air, solid waste and the science underneath them.

lesson.title: Water Chemistry and Microbiology
lesson.summary: The science under the tap — equilibrium, reaction rates and the microbes treatment must remove.

lesson.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment
lesson.summary: The treatment train — from coagulation basins to disinfection and the biology of activated sludge.

lesson.title: Hydrology and Hydraulics
lesson.summary: Water's movement at scale — runoff, channels, pipes and aquifers.

lesson.title: Air Quality Engineering
lesson.summary: Cleaning a moving fluid — dispersion modelling and the scrubbers, filters and cyclones of air control.

lesson.title: Solid and Hazardous Waste Engineering
lesson.summary: Waste as an engineering object — landfills, materials recovery and cleaning up the past.

lesson.title: Sustainability Engineering
lesson.summary: Engineering the transition — carbon accounting, renewables integration and designing for a changed climate.

source.board: National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (NCEES)
source.qualification: NCEES FE Industrial and Systems CBT Exam Specifications
source.track: professional licensure · Fundamentals of Engineering (Industrial & Systems)

industrial-engineering.note: Units follow the NCEES FE Industrial & Systems specification's knowledge areas — probability and statistics through facilities, human factors and operations.

lesson.title: Statistics, Quality and Control Charts
lesson.summary: Engineering variation itself — distributions, control charts and the statistics of acceptable quality.

lesson.title: Optimisation and Operations Research
lesson.summary: Decision-making as mathematics — linear programmes, networks and the simplex method's guarantees.

lesson.title: Facilities and Layout Design
lesson.summary: Designing where work happens — layout types, line balancing and where to put the plant.

lesson.title: Human Factors and Work Design
lesson.summary: The human as system component — motion studies, ergonomics and designing for attention and error.

lesson.title: Production Planning and Inventory Systems
lesson.summary: Coordinating production — scheduling, MRP logic, JIT and the mathematics of stock.

lesson.title: Simulation and Queuing Analysis
lesson.summary: Testing decisions before reality — queuing maths and discrete-event simulation of whole systems.

source.qualification: ABET Program Criteria — Petroleum and Similarly Named Engineering Programs

petroleum-engineering.note: Units follow ABET's required petroleum curriculum areas — drilling, reservoir, production and the economics and ethics of extraction.

lesson.title: Petroleum Geology and Reservoir Rock
lesson.summary: Where oil lives — source rocks, traps and the porosity–permeability pairs that make a reservoir.

lesson.title: Drilling Engineering
lesson.summary: Making the hole — rig systems, drilling mud, cementing and keeping the well under control.

lesson.title: Reservoir Engineering
lesson.summary: How hydrocarbons flow to the well — Darcy's law, drive mechanisms and enhanced recovery.

lesson.title: Production Engineering
lesson.summary: Keeping oil flowing — completions, artificial lift, hydraulic fracturing and flow assurance.

lesson.title: Formation Evaluation
lesson.summary: Measuring what you cannot see — well logs, cores and the arithmetic of reserves.

units.title: Economics, safety and the energy transition

lesson.title: Economics, Safety and the Transition
lesson.summary: Petroleum engineering's wider frame — project economics, safety culture and the subsurface skills of the energy transition.

source.qualification: ABET Program Criteria — Nuclear and Similarly Named Engineering Programs

nuclear-engineering.note: Units follow ABET's required nuclear curriculum areas — radiation science, reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, safety and the fuel cycle.

lesson.title: Radiation Physics and Detection
lesson.summary: The physics underneath — decay chains, how radiation interacts with matter and how it is measured.

lesson.title: Reactor Physics
lesson.summary: Keeping a chain reaction exactly critical — neutron balance, reactivity coefficients and control.

units.title: Nuclear power systems
topics: Steam cycles and balance of plant

lesson.title: Nuclear Power Plant Systems
lesson.summary: From fission to the grid — reactor types, steam cycles and the new generation of small reactors.

lesson.title: Thermal-hydraulics of Reactors
lesson.summary: Removing heat that will not switch off — coolant behaviour, boiling and decay heat after shutdown.

lesson.title: Nuclear Safety and Shielding
lesson.summary: Engineering against the worst day — defence in depth, shielding maths and the licensing process.

lesson.title: The Fuel Cycle and Fusion's Frontier
lesson.summary: Nuclear's full arc — the fuel cycle, long-lived waste and the engineering of fusion power.

source.qualification: MIT OpenCourseWare operations research curriculum (15.093 / ORC)

operations-research.note: Units follow the OR curriculum's canonical arc — optimisation first (linear, integer, nonlinear), then probability in queues and simulation, then decision analysis.

units.title: Linear programming and the simplex method

lesson.title: Linear Programming
lesson.summary: Optimising with lines and half-spaces — formulation, the simplex method and what duality really says.

lesson.title: Network Flow Algorithms
lesson.summary: Optimisation on graphs — shortest paths, the max-flow/min-cut theorem and transport problems.

lesson.title: Integer Optimisation
lesson.summary: When decisions are yes/no — branch and bound, cutting planes and living with NP-hardness.

lesson.title: Nonlinear Optimisation
lesson.summary: Curved landscapes — convexity's guarantees, gradient descent and the KKT conditions.

units.title: Probability models: queues and Markov chains

lesson.title: Queues and Markov Models
lesson.summary: Waiting as mathematics — Poisson arrivals, the M/M/1 queue and decisions under Markov uncertainty.

lesson.title: Simulation and Decision Analysis
lesson.summary: Deciding with simulations — Monte Carlo, decision trees and choosing among competing objectives.

landscape-architecture.note: Units follow LAAB's required content areas — design studios and theory, plants and ecology, construction technology, and planning and professional practice.

lesson.title: Landscape Design Process
lesson.summary: Reading land as a designer — site analysis, the studio method and the canon of landscape design.

lesson.title: Planting Design and Ecology
lesson.summary: Choosing living material — plant communities, water in the landscape and restoration practice.

lesson.title: Landscape Construction and Grading
lesson.summary: Building outdoor rooms — grading maths, construction detailing and water as a design material.

lesson.title: Urban Landscape Design
lesson.summary: Landscapes at city scale — parks, streets and the cooling power of green infrastructure.

lesson.title: Landscape Planning and Analysis
lesson.summary: Beyond the site — regional planning, heritage landscapes and geospatial analysis.

lesson.title: Professional Landscape Practice
lesson.summary: The profession — contracts, licensure and measuring whether landscapes actually perform.

source.board: National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (NCEES)
source.qualification: NCEES FS (Fundamentals of Surveying) exam specifications

surveying.note: Units follow the NCEES FS specification's knowledge areas — basic sciences and maths through measurement, positioning, law and the business of surveying.

lesson.title: Surveying Mathematics
lesson.summary: The maths under every measurement — trigonometry, error propagation and the shape of the Earth.

lesson.title: Measurement Instruments
lesson.summary: The instrument kit — total stations, EDM and the art of levelling.

lesson.title: Satellite Positioning (GNSS)
lesson.summary: Knowing where you are to centimetres — how GNSS works and why base stations matter.

lesson.title: Boundaries and the Law
lesson.summary: Where law meets land — deeds, monuments and the detective work of retracement.

lesson.title: Topographic and Construction Surveying
lesson.summary: Surveying in production — mapping terrain and putting designs on the ground.

lesson.title: Modern Surveying: Drones, LiDAR and GIS
lesson.summary: The profession today — photogrammetry, laser scanning and managing geospatial data.
